case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: In a foster-care class action the court recognized that foster children hold a substantive due process right to be free from unreasonable risk of harm and to reasonable safety, but held the jury was misinstructed by treating the professional-judgment standard of care as the right itself, and it narrowed the systemwide injunction.
key_cases.relevance: The court dismissed most federal child welfare statutory claims, showing the limits of privately enforcing federal compliance standards.
key_cases.quote: We hold that foster children have a constitutional substantive due process right to be free from unreasonable risks of harm and a right to reasonable safety.

key_cases.holding: The court adopted a broad reading of the ICWA and WICWA inquiry threshold, holding that a court has reason to know a child is an Indian child whenever any participant in the proceeding indicates the child has tribal heritage, and that the trial court had reason to know at the shelter care hearing.
key_cases.relevance: Failure to apply the correct reason-to-know standard is itself a compliance failure requiring reversal.
key_cases.quote: We hold that a trial court has "reason to know" that a child is an Indian child when a participant in the proceeding indicates that the child has tribal heritage.

key_cases.holding: The court held that the ICWA active-efforts showing under 25 U.S.C. section 1912(d) need be proved only by clear, cogent and convincing evidence rather than beyond a reasonable doubt, and that a parent's voluntary unavailability excuses the State from offering further remedial services.
key_cases.relevance: Identifies which ICWA findings carry the beyond-a-reasonable-doubt standard and which do not, a frequent source of compliance error.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the trial court properly applied the clear, cogent and convincing standard to the requirements contained in 25 U.S.C. § 1912(d).
